items.q: How do you say 'I'm going to Berlin' (by train) in German?
items.why: Students use gehen for any 'going'. In German, gehen = go ON FOOT only. FAHREN = go by vehicle (car, train, bus). FLIEGEN = go by plane. To Berlin by train: ich fahre. Saying 'ich gehe nach Berlin' suggests walking there!
Students use English -s plural. German has multiple plural patterns including UMLAUT + er for many masculine nouns: Mann to Männer, Buch to Bücher, Land to Länder. Plurals must often be memorised.

items.misconception: Accusative (because it sounds like a direct relationship).
items.why: Students guess case based on logic. Mit is a DATIVE preposition - one of several you memorise (aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu - mnemonic). Each preposition has a fixed case.

items.q: What is the correct reflexive pronoun: 'ich verstehe ___ gut mit meinen Eltern'?
items.why: It's mich. “mir” is the classic near-miss here; knowing why it's wrong is worth as much as knowing the right answer.

items.q: When was Ehe für alle introduced?
items.why: The answer examiners want is: 2017. “2001” is the distractor this question was built around — if it tempted you, that's the exact gap to close.

items.q: Up to how many months of Elterngeld can a couple receive (basic Elterngeld)?
items.why: Exact answer: 14 months. Estimation gets you near it; only the anchored number survives the exam hall.
